sections.h2: Unsegregated Indian waste often falls at or below the incineration floor

chart.title: Unsegregated waste's energy content frequently sits at or below the 1,500 kcal/kg floor
chart.source: Figures as cited in the post.

sections.means: Unsegregated Indian municipal waste typically ranges from 800 to 2,150 kcal/kg, while the legal floor for energy recovery is 1,500 kcal/kg.
sections.todo: Segregate wet waste at source so the residual stream clears the 1,500 kcal/kg floor before it reaches an incinerator.

sections.h2: India's waste-to-energy capacity reached only 250–300 MW against an 800 MW target

chart.title: By 2020, installed waste-to-energy capacity was 250–300 MW of the 800 MW target
chart.source: Figures as cited in the post.

sections.means: India's 2018-19 target of 800 MW of waste-to-energy capacity had reached only 250–300 MW installed by 2020.
sections.todo: Tie waste-to-energy financing to sorted feedstock so plants receive fuel that matches the calorific value they are built for.

sections.h2: Seven of roughly 15 Indian waste-to-energy plants built since 1987 have shut down

chart.title: Seven of roughly 15 plants closed, largely over the calorific-value shortfall
chart.sub: Indian waste-to-energy plants built since 1987, count.
chart.source: Figures as cited in the post.

sections.means: Of roughly 15 waste-to-energy plants India has built since 1987, seven have shut down, a failure rate above 45%.
sections.todo: Make source sorting a condition of waste-to-energy financing so plants are fed waste that clears the calorific floor.
